ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is circle J, and point J is marked inside the circle and serves as the center of the circle. On the left side there is vertical chord GH; radius/segment JR goes from the center J perpendicular to chord GH, with foot R, and JR is labeled 5. In the lower right there is chord KL; segment JS goes from the center J perpendicular to chord KL, with foot S, and JS is also labeled 5. There are right-angle marks at R and S in the figure. Reasoning: In the same circle, two chords that are equal distances from the center of the circle are equal. Because JR = 5 and JS = 5, the perpendicular distances from chords GH and KL to the center of the circle are equal, therefore GH = KL. The problem gives GH = 9, KL = 4x + 1, so 9 = 4x + 1. Solving gives 4x = 8, x = 2.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: J is the center of circle J, segment JR is perpendicular to chord GH at R, segment JS is perpendicular to chord KL at S, and the diagram labels JR = 5 and JS = 5. From the text, use GH = 9 and KL = 4x + 1. Since chords in the same circle that are the same perpendicular distance from the center are congruent, GH = KL. Set 9 = 4x + 1 and solve to get x = 2.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: J is the circle center, JR is perpendicular to chord GH and JS is perpendicular to chord KL; both distances from the center to the chords are marked 5. A radius from J to an endpoint of either chord would form a right triangle whose leg from the center to the chord is 5 and whose other leg is half the chord length. Because both triangles use the same circle radius as hypotenuse and the same center-to-chord distance 5 as one leg, their half-chord lengths must be equal. Therefore the full chords GH and KL are equal. From the text, GH = 9 and KL = 4x + 1, so 4x + 1 = 9, giving x = 2.
